\begin{table*}[t]
\caption{Altitude acquisition and hold. Every episode starts $\Delta\sim\pm\,\mathcal{U}(12,18)$~m off the commanded altitude, in both directions, at commanded altitudes of 20--100~m, and all five controllers track the identical rate-limited acquisition reference. Surv. is the fraction of episodes that reach the horizon without a crash or a stall, and Acq. the fraction that additionally reach and hold the target to within 1~m. Error metrics are means over the surviving episodes, and $n$ is the number of episodes in each sweep. The learned rows are means over three training seeds, and every metric is quoted as mean $\pm$ standard deviation across them; a method flown once carries no spread. The LQR is a deterministic law and is swept once; MPPI is a sampling planner and a single sweep is one draw, so it is swept three times and averaged the same way as the learned methods. The learned policies and MPPI are scored on the GPU plant and the LQR on the CPU reference plant, which are validated to single-step parity (Section~\ref{sec:validation}) but are not the same code path.}

\begin{table*}[t]
\caption{Attitude-stream tracking across the four named maneuvers: bank-angle RMSE in degrees as mean $\pm$ standard deviation across runs, with the time-in-band percentage in brackets. All five methods drive the identical $(\phi^\star,\dot h^\star,V_a^\star)$ stream through the same plant. The learned methods are flown once per training seed and averaged over three seeds, as in Table~\ref{tab:altitude-protocol}. MPPI has no seeds, but a single rollout is one draw, so it is flown five times with different sampling seeds. The LQR is a deterministic law, is flown once and carries no spread.
